entries.appliesTo: local school boards / public school divisions (plus federal-funds-accepting private schools for filtering)

dutySources.registration-filing: § 22.1-70.2(A) — 'each local school division shall certify compliance with these requirements annually to the Department of Education'

sources.curriculum: § 22.1-70.2(A)(v) — 'include a component on internet safety for students that is integrated in a division's instructional program that includes instruction on key modern digital safety topics, including online scams, misinformation, and content generated by artificial intelligence'
sources.policyRequired: § 22.1-70.2(A) — 'Every two years, each local school board shall review, amend if necessary, and approve the school division's acceptable use policy for the internet.'

flags: AI is one topic among several: the amendment adds 'online scams, misinformation, and content generated by artificial intelligence' to an existing internet-safety instruction component; most of § 22.1-70.2 (policy adoption, filtering, certification) is pre-existing law reenacted here

no penalty or enforcement provision aimed at the statute itself; subsection B only directs the division superintendent to 'implement and enforce the division's policy' against users — exposure omitted (silence is silence)

subsection D imposes a duty on the Superintendent of Public Instruction to 'issue guidelines to school divisions... that includes guidance on the topics specified in clause (v) of subsection A' — a state-agency (public-sector) duty not captured by education-k12 params

subsection C requires private schools that satisfy compulsory attendance and accept federal funds for internet access to filter child pornography and obscenity — a filtering duty (pre-existing, not AI-related) with no matching duty key in the vocabulary
